questions.question: How do you usually get the news, and how often do you check it?
questions.model_answer: I usually listen to a short radio news summary while I make breakfast. At night, I read one or two articles on my phone, so I check the news about twice a day.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a news magazine is researching media habits in your country. You agreed to take part in a telephone interview about the ways people get the news.
questions.question: Do you prefer short news updates or longer reports? Why?
questions.model_answer: I prefer short updates on an ordinary day. I choose a longer report only when the story will affect my work or my city directly.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a news magazine is researching media habits in your country. You agreed to take part in a telephone interview about the ways people get the news.
questions.question: Some people check the news many times a day. Do you think that is a good habit? Why or why not?
questions.model_answer: I do not think checking the news many times a day is a good habit. Headlines rarely change between morning and lunch, and constant checking adds worry without new facts. Twice a day keeps me informed and still able to finish my work. If something urgent happens, one alert is enough. Until then, I stay with the task in front of me.

questions.question: Do you agree that every workplace should set aside a quiet place for focused work? Support your view with reasons and an example.
questions.model_answer: I agree that every workplace should set aside a quiet place for focused work. Open rooms help with quick teamwork, but they are a poor place to write, calculate, or learn a new task, because each nearby voice breaks your concentration. A small room, booked for an hour, lets someone finish that work and then rejoin the group. At my last job, people stayed late just to find silence, which was unfair to anyone expected at home. The room does not need to be fancy. It needs a door, a desk, and a rule that phones stay silent. That simple space would help people do better work in fewer hours, and it would cost a company very little compared with what it gives back.
